items.title: Pane: Attached Projects/Sparks/Files/Folders
items.description: Make it so you can see the attached files and folders and projects and sparks and (etc.,) in this pane.

items.title: Panel Titles
items.description: We need to be able to name the whiteboards (and broadly, panels in general).  Where it says "Whiteboard" right now, needs to be editable, and it will form the logical title.

items.title: Data (Object?) Panels
items.notes:
For example, -- links?

Perhaps they are TkMarkup panels, or similar -- using the data-vs-display/edit juxtaposition, ...

What if some data is actually external?  Like, a link in a link database, but the link database is external to Today?

What about data objects like: Songs I am listening to.  Artist, song, album, URL to YouTube, or it's location elsewhere, ...

items.title: Whiteboards From Previous Pages
items.description:
Make it so that you can paste the GUID of a panel on another page, or perhaps the date of another page, so that you can load it into mem and access it?

Need to think about -- Epochs vs. Days vs. Panels; this would be a major reorganization.

items.description: a wiki-like syntax for pane contents -- use for todos and other things

items.title: Image Panels
items.description: Be able to have a panel that is an image captured from the clipboard.

items.title: Expand Beyond Today: "Everything with a Cockpit"
items.description: I've noticed that the "cockpit" system would be useful for more than just tracking notes on dates -- it seems that projects, notes on various subjects, -- myriad things would benefit from this kind of a panel layout.
items.notes: UNCLEAR WHETHER TO DO THIS OR NOT.

items.title: Journal and Log Notes
items.description: This would be an upward scrolling log, and you could read it backwards.  Log entries could exported.  Log entries could be tagged by pressing depressable buttons, and you should be able to add tag sets.  You just type into the bar, and it becomes a time-stamped log note.  You should be able to delete or edit previous log notes.  You should also be able to use a more editor-like interface (basically, a Text window, and a small Text area for editing tags.)  Think Tweets with occasional Blog entries.
items.notes: Perhaps if you use a tag, the rest of the entries for the day could take up that tag...
